A supposed Pokemon 'leak' account has admitted to faking rumors about Pokemon Winds and Waves, saying that they'd "do it again."

Drama kicked off earlier this week when screenshots surfaced showing the Twitter account @kurwashibamaste – which had become the source for a number of rumors reposted by prominent leaks, and rumors account @CentroLeaks – on the same list of logged-in accounts as @Mootmonthly, previously thought to be a separate individual.

This raised a few eyebrows, but especially when Moot shared a new post – a GIF of beloved Jujutsu Kaisen character Nanami looking blissful with the caption, "How it feels to spread misinformation and lies."

In the replies, Moot says: "The actual community fallout isn't really relevant to me; i set out to accomplish a specific goal with kurwa and i got it done relatively quickly. Having fun with the larp was just gravy." They believe that their "rep was a little too good" which apparently "forces one into being rather limited in what they can say/post." Instead, they say: "I vastly would prefer being viewed as a clown."

But what was the goal? In a separate thread, Moot says: "I was investigating how much all of the 'leakers' actually knew and how they knew it. Results were rather disappointing."

As part of that, they claim that "not everything" posted on the Kurwashibamaste account was made up – "the entire reason the thing worked was because I posted real stuff that they picked up on."

With that said, it doesn't sound like debunking fake leaks was Moot's only motive. Asked why they'd lie, they respond: "Gets me leaks and I'll do it again." Acknowledging the backlash they're now facing online, Moot says: "All in the name of the game big dawg."

Sign up to our Switch 2 Spotlight newsletter to make sure you get the very latest news on Nintendo's new console and its games every week

Obviously, though, the outcome is that a bunch of rumors and supposed leaks about Pokemon Winds and Waves that surfaced in recent months have now seemingly been debunked. Claims that Onix, Salandit, Zweilous, and Houndour were set to receive new regional evolutions, for example, and that there'd be no new Eevee evolution, appear to have been fabricated. Not via the Kurwashibamaste account, but Moot also recently claimed that Winds and Waves were originally supposed to launch in 2026 before an internal delay pushed them back to 2027, the window that The Pokemon Company officially announced a few months ago.

If nothing else, this is a good reminder not to believe everything you see from supposed leak accounts on social media. Based on Moot's recent posts, it sounds like they're planning to release a video sharing the findings of their "investigation" into other apparent leakers, so we may see even more supposed Winds and Waves info debunked soon.

After less than 6 years, Pokemon Unite is shutting down, but it's getting a feature that'll let you hold onto your progress even after the servers are dead.

#3853. Embracer begin yet another round of layoffs at Crystal Dynamics, while they're still midway through development on two Tomb Raider games

Update: Studio confirms eight staff lost their jobs

Update 18/11: Crystal Dynamics have provided the following statement to RPS, confirming it cut eight staff members:

As initially reported by Vertical Slice (thanks, Chris!), the workforce of Tomb Raider studio Crystal Dynamics is being cut as part of a new set of layoffs by owners Embracer. As far as is currently known, those affected include senior game designer Joshua Mitchell, senior environment technical artist Kevin Baker, and UI software engineer Garin R. K. Richards, all of whom shared news of their redunancies on LinkedIn. There may be more affected, but neither Crystal Dynamics nor Embracer have offered comments on the reduction of staff as yet.

This now marks the studio's fifth round of layoffs since Embracer acquired it in 2022, following cuts in March 2025, August 2025, November 2025, and March this year. This is a drastic amount even considering the current state of the industry, with layoffs seemingly happening several times a week, but unfortunately, this is par for the course for Embracer. Even still, it makes one wonder just how many staff are left at Crystal Dynamics by now. Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis and Tomb Raider: Catalyst are still in production, so you'd hope that the studio won't be shuttered entirely.

According to Legacy of Atlantis' Steam page, generative AI has been used in the development of Legacy of Atlantis "to support some early exploration and temporary development content. Any AI-assisted assets were either replaced or refined by humans in order to maintain the creative and artistic vision of the development team." I would hope that this isn't a case of Embracer cutting staff in the misguided hope that they can just be replaced with the use of genAI, but who can say. Solidarity to those affected, who I hope can find new work soon.

#3852. The next Xbox, Project Helix, is a console and "not a PC" says Microsoft, as it clarifies that computational power isn't sole focus this time

"It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering."

Microsoft has stressed that its next-generation Xbox console, Project Helix, "is not a PC that can also play console games", but rather "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC". The company has also underlined the importance of using gen-AI-adjacent "neural rendering" technology going forwards, and a desire to remove "all the barriers of play that have historically existed" - notably in making the past generations of games playable.

The details come from a Microsoft-produced Xbox magazine made available digitally yesterday, and a Helix-related feature speaking to Xbox vice president of next generation, Jason Ronald. "When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine," Ronald said, "one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games.

"We're very clear on the design goal," Ronald later added. "Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customisability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it."

Notably, Ronald seemed to suggest that Helix - the console, not the handheld; "Helix" refers to a couple of machines - isn't solely focused on computational grunt. Indeed, he said the next generation wasn't about hitting 8K resolutions and 240 hertz frame-rates, but instead leaning on technologies like "neural rendering" - i.e. generative-AI - and encouraging innovation.

"It's about deeper immersion," Ronald said. "It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering to deliver a new level of visual fidelity in more efficient and innovative ways. It's about new kinds of games and new game experiences that we haven't been able to do before. What excites me about the future is the idea of entirely new types of games that have never been possible before, delivered through all the innovation in the silicon and the hardware and the platform that we're delivering."

While referencing the global component shortage and exorbitant prices of computer hardware, he added: "This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years."

Xbox boss Asha Sharma also recently talked up the importance of generative-AI-sounding technology in Xbox's future, saying "too many ideas never become games", and that "a single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations".

Another key part of Xbox's Helix vision is compatibility and game preservation. "Game preservation is core to Xbox," Ronald went as far as to say. "Not only do we feel like it's the right thing for the industry, we feel a deep responsibility as one of its biggest platforms and publishers. For the first 30 years of game development, nobody really thought about game preservation when they were designing their hardware, when they were building their games." Xbox is apparently working with game-makers to ensure games can not only be played now but also 20 to 30 years into the future.

The other key facet of Microsoft's push the familiar Play Anywhere mantra, whereby one game can be played across multiple devices, maintaining your game-progress as you go. This is fundamental to Microsoft's handheld-and-console Helix plan, and something we've seen the company dry-run with the Xbox ROG Ally X handheld. "It's this notion that not only does my library move with me, but my progress moves with me as well," Ronald said. "Because I fully expect that when I'm in the middle of an 80-hour RPG, if I'm 25 hours into that and I want to play it on another device, I should be able to instantly resume from where I was. Those are things that today are becoming more common, but I think in the future it's going to be a baseline expectation of all players."

Ronald wouldn't be drawn on the issue of price regarding Project Helix - a recent report suggested Helix could be priced up to $1800 - referring to it only as both "a challenging time" but an "exciting one", because "we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable". Ronald also wouldn't reference a release date, though the report referenced above suggested the handheld Helix machine will release next holiday, 2027, and the console Helix machine the year after. The next generation, then, seems to be around the corner.

Having to refuel cars in GTA 6 was weirdly one of the most talked about features before launch—I guess people didn't like the idea of having to pull over for gas while being chased by half the Vice City's police department. But the reality is that refuelling cars is something you'll barely find yourself doing.

When your ride does run low on fuel, you can find a gas station on the map via the gas pump symbols:

Easy, right? And you'll barely have to do it since, just like real life, cars can go quite a long time without refuelling if they have a full tank, even if you're going over 60mph, which I assume you are. Note that if you steal a stranger's car, their tank may nearly be empty already.

If you're driving an electric car, check the map for recharging stations. Pull up close to one, select "Charge Vehicle," and it'll display the cost. You'll see a quick scene of the readout on the charging station filling the battery to 100%, and when it's done, you can drive away.

Now, the better reason to visit Vice City's fuel stations is that they can repair your vehicle, and if you drive like I do, you'll need this a lot. This is a separate interaction at the same gas pump: on the"Services" menu, just select "Repair" instead. The camera will whoosh into the sky for a moment, and when it returns to ground level your ride will be fixed.

The cost depends on how much damage you've done to your vehicle, but it's well worth it if you want to retain your ride, considering the usual vehicular wear-and-tear that comes with being a professional criminal.

Since you can customise your beloved vehicles at the Mod Shop, or even claim fancier cars by removing their trackers at the Pay 'n' Spray, once you unlock this in the story, keeping your car in good condition is a worthwhile investment.

#3850. Can GTA 6 make $2 billion in its opening weekend? One industry analyst has run the numbers, and seems to think so

We all know the story of GTA 5 making more than $1 billion in the first three days it was on sale, right? At the time, Take-Two believed this to be the fastest any entertainment property had achieved the impressive milestone - music and films included. It made history, and with ease. And it looks like GTA 6 is going to do even better.

At least, that's according to one analyst, Joost van Dreunen, a senior data analyst and great writer/numbers diviner who wrote some predictions in his respected SuperJoost PlayList newsletter. "My prediction: Take-Two announces opening-weekend sales above $2 billion by Monday, 23rd November," he wrote. And you know what? I reckon he's onto something.

Let's review what we already know: there is a conservative estimate of 10 million pre-orders for Rockstar's latest game floating around - something buoyed by comments from Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick - and, even by the company's lofty expectations, we know the game is tracking "well above expectations" when it comes to pre-orders.

We also know a lot of people are shelling out for the slightly more pricey Ultimate Edition (£90). So many people are opting for the more expensive version, in fact, that Take-Two revised its financial forecast up to $3.5bn for the next financial quarter, thanks to "recurrent consumer spending" (something Zelnick clarified in an investor's call is explicitly linked to the Ultimate Edition). 10 million pre-orders, at roughly $100 per copy - that's $1 billion right off the bat.

"That’s two days faster than its predecessor," van Dreunen said, "and largely before anyone has even played the game." That other $1bn will come over the weekend. And then, per the analyst, the game will sell roughly another 28 million copies over the course of the first year it's on sale. "My forecast puts first-year sales at 38 million copies, only modestly ahead of GTA 5’s 35 million. The real difference may be how much revenue each player generates over the years that follow."

But it's what follows in the newsletter that intrigues me most. "At the high end, [GTA 6] may just lift the entire industry with it," wrote van Dreunen. "In the face of AI slop and shitty mobile games that exist only to extract revenue, it will offer a reprieve. At a time when the industry is increasingly focused on making games cheaper and monetising players more aggressively, Rockstar is about to demonstrate the enduring appeal of spending a fortune to make something people actually want to play."

So, even if you're dubious about the game and Rockstar's motivations for selling as many copies as possible, the launch of GTA 6 could be something that gives the industry a much-needed jolt of life, in the face of rampant layoffs and shrinking talent pools.

It's not all sunshine and rainbows ahead for Rockstar, though: amongst the frenzy of launch activity, Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week, as the game goes on sale.

#3849. Sony defeat $2.6 billion UK class action lawsuit which argued PlayStation's dominant market position fuels "excessive and unfair" game prices

It's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony. A UK class action lawsuit which accused the company of using the PlayStation Store's dominant market position to fuel "excessive and unfair" prices for digital games has been dismissed in its entirety by the Competition Appeal Tribunal in London.

As reported by Reuters and The Game Business, the body ruled that the lawsuit - brought by Alex Neill on behalf of folks who bought digital games on PlayStation between August 2016 and February 2026 - failed to establish that Sony had infringed competition law.

The lawsuit claimed that PlayStation's dominant position when it comes to selling digital games on its platforms via the PlayStation Store subjected consumers to "excessive and unfair prices", as a result of terms and a 30% commission fee levied against developers. Neill and co argued owning a PlayStation traps game buyers within a competitionless ecosystem, thereby impacting their ability to seek out a better deal.

It's quite similar to the arguments which have been made against Valve in similar lawsuits concerning the Steam overlords' dominance over the PC game buying space, though a key distinction is that there is some competition on PC via the likes of the Epic store and GOG. How effective some of that competition can be in practice is a different kettle of fish, but the options are there.

In a judgement that could potentially factor into the responses to any similar lawsuits against Valve or other PC storefronts going forwards, the tribunal ruled that Sony compete in a wider ‘systems market’ against Xbox, Nintendo and PC, with PlayStation having no legal duty under competition law to allow third-party stores onto their platform as competition closer to home. The latter the tribunal noted would be expensive, complex and come with potential security ramifications.

As if that wasn't enough, the body ruled that as far as the pricing being unfair went, Neill hadn't proven that Sony’s profit margins were excessive and declared there was no evidence the presence of rival storefronts on PlayStation would've seen prices come down. That's essentially the word NO written in the largest font possible on a sheet of paper the size of a table, then.

Every lawsuit's different, especially when filed in different countries, but if I was one of the other class action suits against Sony or another big game seller on the go at the moment, I'd maybe not be feeling so hot right now. On the other hand, perhaps seeing what the tribunal judged Neill not to have provided suffiencient evidence for might aid those other efforts in formulating their arguments ready to face the scrutiny of government bodies and corporate law-talkers.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Selling stolen goods in GTA 6 is a core part of the day-to-day experience in Leonida. It's your primary way of making money in GTA 6, and will be an essential way of unlocking all of the great cars, clothes, and weapons that you want to own. Of course, you can't just take any hot items down to your local pawn shop to make some quick cash – you'll need to take narcotics, jewellery, and marked bills to specific fences and vendors.

Below I'm going to help you understand how to fence stolen goods in GTA 6, and give you a better sense of what the potential takeaways and pitfalls from key vendors are likely to be.

This process is different from how to sell cars in GTA 6, but we've got a guide on that if you want to truly engage in the process of grand theft auto.

If you're setting your sights beyond sticking up convenience stores and innocent civilians on the streets, you'll quickly find that you have scores which need to be laundered through specific fences. The first of these that you'll unlock is Brian's Lockup in South Key Lento, which you can unlock in the mission "Lab Fees".

When you drop off stolen goods, it will take a certain amount of time for the money to be sent to your mailbox. Depending on the fence, it may take several days!

You will unlock different fences as you progress through the GTA 6 missions list, with each offering a speciality service and more lucrative returns on stolen goods. If you don't have great fences available, your best bet is to continue with the story and make more criminal contacts.Let's understand what kind of stolen goods each class of Robbery in the GTA 6 index will give you:

From that Index, you can head to the Robberies section and scroll down to the part where it says "Drop-offs – Goods". These are the fences that you have available to you at that point in the story. If you hover over each one (if you're still in Chapter 1, you'll have locations for Brian and Donnie as options) the game will explain what items you have stashed on your person which can be sold, and what price a fence will offer for your narcotics, jewellery, and marked bills.

Different fences will offer different prices for these goods (ranging from Very Low > Low > Medium > High > Very High) so it's worth your time coordinating if you can, unless your GTA 6 Wanted Level is out of control of course. At the beginning of the game, you'll need to drive to the specific drop-off spot to sell your entire stash, but other drop-off opportunities become available in the later game.

#3846. Only two days out from GTA 6, its publisher Take-Two lay off staff at XCOM and Civilization developer Firaxis

About a third of the workforce has been cut, reportedly

Upsettingly, it is that time of the week again, as Take-Two are laying off staff at Firaxis, the developer behind Civilization and XCOM, only a little over a year the last time the studio suffered from layoffs. Firaxis are, notably, owned by Take-Two, the publisher of GTA 6 which comes out in, oh, two days time? Interesting timing, 'ey.

Word of the layoffs came from Bloomberg, who report that about 60 people are losing their jobs, apparently roughly a third of its staff. The studio's head, Heather Hazen, is also leaving. A spokesperson for 2K Games (the Take-Two label that manages Firaxis) shared a statement on the layoffs: "Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength - designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years.

"As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis." I don't feel personally confident in the idea that the only way to make a company succeed is by laying a bunch of people off thereby making it much harder to make anything in the first place, especially in the lead-up to what will likely be the best selling game of the decade, but what do I know!

Bloomberg also report Firaxis have been working on a new XCOM, which is yet to be announced, but the project has apparently had to contend with numerous development issues, missing a "significant milestone over the summer." This new XCOM game hasn't been cancelled at the very least, but anonymous sources that spoke with Bloomberg said it may have to deal with a shakeup due to the cuts. As always, solidarity with all those affected by this situation.

#3845. Ever wanted to play a multiplayer version of Cyberpunk 2077 with your friends? Well, thanks to a mod now in beta, you can

You may have recently read that CD Projekt Red's in-development Cyberpunk 2 may be trying to revive the original game's online ambitions. But, if you don't want to wait the many years it'll likely be before the Cyberpunk 2077 sequel arrives, then I've got good news for you: Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta.

"After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders on the CyberMP Discord channel wrote (thanks RPS). "Anyone can jump in and play now - no invites or applications needed." The team notes, however, that this is "true beta", meaning "Crashes, desyncs, and server drops under heavy load are completely normal for now. That's exactly why we need testers."

Alongside the potential shakiness, the devs say it's also possible the mod could ping your anti-virus software, since it "doesn't have a digital signature yet". Whilst the priorities for the team lie in "polishing the foundations" and "fixing crashes and stability", more features are eventually planned. But for now, they stress, "let's see how the project handles real player traffic!"

So, what exactly is it? CyberMP is a dedicated multiplayer modification for Cyberpunk 2077 that allows you and your friends to explore Night City together: drive vehicles, engage in combat, and play custom community-created game modes on high-tick dedicated servers. You need an official copy of the game to play it (obviously), and the mod is completely free to download. You can download the mod, and read a fair amount of how to get it working, what to expect from it, and how to troubleshoot any issues, over at its dedicated website.

If you're thinking 'Hang on, why does Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer sound so familiar?', it's because the game was supposed to receive an official multiplayer mode after its original release. Thanks to its shaky launch, however, plans changed, and CD Projekt Red later announced that multiplayer would be a separate "triple-A release", but, eventually, that too was cancelled. The studio is still keen to honour the idea, though, and recently stated it's "focusing on bringing online into all of our franchises one day".

This isn't the first big bit of news we've had about Cyberpunk 2077 mods this week. Just yesterday, a new mod called 'Torrent' added 3D rain, lightning storms, and tyre spray to Night City - all rendered and made lovely with a new lighting system that seems to play nicely with other weather mods that have been created for the game.

Remember how stealing a cop car in the older GTA games used to get you a free shotgun? Well, turns out Vice City's police force is even better armed. If you need some extra guns quickly, particularly shotguns and assault rifles, filching them from the trunk of a police car is a great method, though obviously it comes with certain risks.

You might have realised, but stealing cars in GTA 6 is significantly more complicated than previous games, especially if they're alarmed. Thankfully, this doesn't apply to any police pickup trucks like the Bravado Bison the cops sometimes use, which you'll spot occasionally both in rural areas and in the city

With the police pickups, you can simply climb onto the bed at the back and open the storage crate, grabbing any weapons and ammo inside, including other potential items like Stun Guns, without setting off any alarms.

For proper police cruisers, though, their trunks are alarmed along with the doors, meaning you'll need a tool to deal with them, the slim jim, which you get during the "Moses" mission in Chapter 2. If you slim jim the door of the cop car and get inside, the trunk will unlock, so you can head around the back, interact to open it, and steal whatever's in the boot without tackling the alarm, whether it be an assault rifle, shotgun, or even body armor.

If you don't have the slim jim yet, you can still open the trunk (you'll see your character use a screwdriver) but the alarm will go off.

Once you've collected the weapons, you can interact with your own car trunk, and you'll see a prompt to stow the weapons inside. You'll be rather conspicuous wandering around with an assault rifle in your hands or strapped to your back, after all.

Obviously, it's best not to try and steal cop cars with cops in them, but you can find them around, or parked at police stations, such as in Port Gellhorn or Vice City.

More generally, it's definitely worth looting random car trunks to see what you can find. Sometimes they contain cash, drugs, handguns, or consumables—just make sure to scan them with the Wainkit App first (which you're introduced to in Chapter 1) to tell if they're alarmed or not, and whether you can break in without the slim jim.

#3843. Saihate Station: Twilight Edition announced for Switch

Publisher PLAYISM and developer viv have announced Saihate Station: Twilight Edition, a Switch version of the 2D exploration horror adventure game including the base game and downloadable content “Twilight Railway,” as well as two mini-games. It will launch on March 25, 2027 worldwide with English, Japanese, Korean, Traditional Chinese, and Simplified Chinese language support. A physical edition will be available in Japan for 8,800 yen.

Saihate Station first launched for PC via Steam on March 7, 2025. The downloadable content “Twilight Railway” launched on April 18, 2025.

Here is an overview of the game, via PLAYISM:

Since its release in March 2025, this 2D exploration horror adventure game has recorded a cumulative series total of 1.6 million downloads, an exceptional achievement for an indie free game, and continues to receive passionate support from fans in Japan and abroad. Now it is finally coming to Nintendo Switch!

Saihate Station: Twilight Edition includes the main game, the downloadable content “Twilight Railway,” and two mini-games, all in one package.

“After falling asleep on the last train, I woke up in a bizarre place called Saihate Station…”

Haru Akinashi is a self-effacing office worker who lacks confidence and fails at everything he tries. Having slept through his stop on the last train, he finds himself trapped in a bizarre place called Saihate Station, where gruesome supernatural phenomena occur.

Shion Tatsunami is his complete opposite: a cheerful, talented colleague and former friend—happens to be there as well, and the two promise to work together to return home.

Their interactions are awkward at first, given the estrangement, but with each problem they overcome together, Haru recalls their former friendship, and their bond grows stronger than before.

The main game features four multiple-ending story routes. The ending branches based on fluctuations in Haru’s “dependency level,” which changes according to the player’s actions.

Starting November 20, pre-orders for the physical edition will begin sequentially at retailers in Japan. As a first-print bonus, a “shaka-shaka acrylic stand keychain” featuring a train and character motif will be included. A limited edition featuring a special box with an “exclusive newly drawn mini-game book” and a “Haru-Shion handkerchief” is also planned. Bonuses and limited editions are available in limited quantities, so please place your pre-order early.

#3842. What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

"We ended up just cutting and cutting it."

It's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto. Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't GTA 6, which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making, with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial production shadowed by labour disputes, that appears to have given Rockstar's various teams little time or space to think about anything else.

It wasn't ever thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption. Once upon a time, they had a reputation for slightly dodgy experiments. I recently interviewed former Rockstar North tech director Obbe Vermeij about a few of them, including Agent, the unofficial James Bond game Rockstar toyed with before putting all chips on Grand Theft Auto 5.

During the noughties especially, when the most expensive games took considerably less time to make, Rockstar tried their hand at a number of projects besides GTA. There was 2002's Manhunt, a rancid parody of snuff films – not much loved, but sufficiently admired to spawn a sequel in the hands of Rockstar London. There was 2005's adaptation of Walter Hill flick The Warriors - a mouthy Homeric beat 'em up in which you cross New York on foot over the course of a single night - and 2006's Rockstar Presents Table Tennis - an inexplicable pivot towards realistic sports simulation from Rockstar San Diego. Later in 2006 came Bully, aka Canis Canem Edit, a boarding school life sim from Rockstar Vancouver (née Barking Dog Studios). I didn't warm to Bully, myself, but I've never been able to get its sardonic OST out of my head.

In amongst all these, Rockstar weighed up several game projects that never made it out of the building. The aforesaid Agent is perhaps the best-known, but my conversation with Vermeij (who worked at Rockstar from 1995 to 2009) began with "Z", a fleeting attempt to expand into the world of zombie action games, which Rockstar spent a few weeks mulling over in the wake of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. It was set in the islands of Scotland, which would have made it the only Rockstar North project to unfold in the studio's backyard. "I think it was meant to be smaller than GTA, map-wise, and there weren't going to be any deserted cities - it was really just islands and some villages," Vermeij told me. "But it really didn't get that far."

The pitch for Z couldn't be further from the sweat and glitter of GTA 6's Miami, but the two projects would have shared a taste for 'simulation' elements. "It actually was going to have cars running out of fuel," Vermeij told me. "That was going to be one of the things, and the whole idea was that you'd find cars and they'd only have a little bit of fuel in them." As for why Z never entered full development, turns out desolate North Atlantic archipelagos full of corpses can be a bit of a downer. "Everybody was super excited to do something new," Vermeij went on. "And then pretty quickly, we kind of realised that it's really just a depressing version of GTA, and it sort of died."

The increasing success of Grand Theft Auto during these years was something of a "curse", Vermeij went on. It meant that a lot of Rockstar's ventures beyond GTA were eventually folded back into the series. "It's very difficult to have a studio and have one mega game, and then do something on the side," he explained. "It's almost impossible, because at any time during the development of the smaller project, management's going to say 'oh! The big project's in trouble. We need more people.' And they're just going to pull everybody from that small team onto the big team, so even if we had progressed with [Z], what would have happened is we would have had to start GTA 4 at the same time, and eventually the small team would just be merged with the big team again."

Rockstar's Bondalike game Agent got a lot further down the road to release than Z. It was in development for several years following GTA 4's launch, and was touted by co-founder Sam Houser as Rockstar's next megagame. "A lot of work had been done on that," Vermeij recalled. "And then we ended up just cutting and cutting it, because the same thing happened – at some point you kind of go OK, well, we better get on with the next GTA."

Agent sounds like it could have been a hoot, at least going by Vermeij's description of his own time with the project. It was a relatively linear, level-based action game with a touch of camp. "There was a French ski resort, and there was going to be a Mediterranean town like San Tropez, somewhere like that," Vermeij explained. "There was going to be a North African place, like Morocco or Egypt. The last level was going to be on the moon, with lasers – like Moonraker. There was another one, London or something, I can't remember. But then we just ended up cutting everything down, because what we could see happening was that at some point, we would have to go back to work on GTA. It wasn't close to being finished."

While never a spoof in the vein of Austin Powers, Agent would have been a sillier production than the grimy and downbeat GTA 4. "It was meant to lean into all the cliches," Vermeij said. "It was like James Bond from the 1970s - there was a girl with white boots. It wasn't a comedy, it was just completely over-the-top cliched."

As for the choice of a level-based format, this came from a desire for variety the studio couldn't realistically achieve in a GTA-style open world. "If you had to have them all on one map, you would basically have had to model a mini version of Europe," Vermeij said, "So you couldn't do that." Players might have been able to revisit locations containing several missions, which calls to mind Io Interactive's later Hitman: World of Assassination games, to say nothing of their own bash at the Flemingverse, 007 First Light. "I don't how whether it was going to be completely linear, or whether you were always going to be able to visit all those locations." Vermeij said.

Needless to say, Rockstar's Bondalike would have featured chase scenes. Vermeij himself worked on the moving parts. "I remember doing some work on what we called the car recording stuff for GTA," he went on. "So if a level designer wanted to set up a chase scene, they would drive one car, record it, and then play back the recording, drive a second car and record that... and so driving one by one, you could set up a whole chase scene. I did a version of that for [human] characters as well, because for one of the Agent missions in the French ski resort, there was like a chase where the bad guys were on skiis and using their machine guns. So I set up a thing where you'd play them one by one, and then play the whole thing back. There was maybe like five or six bad guys and they'd ski after you, and then it was just up to the player to avoid them."

According to Vermeij, Agent never had a defined story during his time with it. It was more of a mix of scenario concepts, "kind of how we used to do games with GTA 3 and Vice City". Mind you, the absence of a nailed-down plot isn't necessarily a sign that Agent was lightyears from being finished. Even at their most byzantine, Bond movie plotlines often feel like an afterthought. "It's like oh yeah, there's a bad guy and there's a thingally-dingally that needs to be captured before the world comes to an end," summarised Vermeij. Still, Agent would spend a long time in limbo after Vermeij left. It's still unclear how much it was in active development before Rockstar's trademark finally evaporated in November 2018.

One thing I learned while reading up on Rockstar's checkered history was that GTA 3, the game that made GTA a Thing on PlayStation, wasn't deemed an immediate hit at launch. According to Vermeij himself, it was months before Rockstar realised what they'd built. This inspired an obvious closing question: what might Rockstar have done, if GTA 3 hadn't blown up the way it did? Which of those other projects might have become the focus?

"I really have never thought about it," Vermeij pondered. "When Rockstar San Diego joined, it was 2002, and they already had a bunch of games and a bunch of franchises, like Midnight Club and Smuggler's Run. They were already into driving games and city games in that way, so it wouldn't have surprised me if we'd gone in that direction anyway. But then they were more about car modding and decals and stuff like that.

"At Rockstar North, we only had Manhunt and GTA," he went on. "With Manhunt, that team was in development hell for a while, they had a couple of rough years where they got stuck and in the end, they pulled through, and they got a pretty decent game. But I don't think that would have been the future. I don't think [Rockstar North] would have done a Manhunt 2. So yeah, it would be Table Tennis, I think! Everything on Table Tennis!"

#3841. World of Warcraft: Forever completionists push back as Blizzard gives them a powerful toy and then prepares to take it away

"Exactly the kind of FOMO that disheartens collectors."

With the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever there's a whole new world filled with niche gear and strange baubles to collect. But one item in particular has drawn the ire of the creators of a popular completionist add-on.

That add-on is All the Things, a must-install for collectors like me, as it acts as a database of all the gear, mounts, titles, crafting recipes, and super rare drops in the game. Once you collect something, it is hidden in the add-on, thus tracking your progress and making for a fantastic tool for picking the game apart.

On occasion, specific items have written notes attached by the All the Things development team, as is true of a special World of Warcraft: Forever toy, the Pouch of Violet Dust. This is a promotional item that was obtainable by watching two hours of WoW Forever streams between the 4th and 12th November.

It's a powerful toy! When used on a campfire, it changes the fire's colour to purple and extends the buffs provided by it from the usual one hour to two hours. But the sticking point with the item isn't its existence, rather the fact that it's going to be removed in early December, not long from now.

This is what the creators of the All the Things add-on don't like. "A week-long, Twitch-only window for an item that gets taken away a month later is exactly the kind of FOMO that disheartens collectors," the creators said in a note attached to the item in the mod. "It can't be earned by playing the game at all. Even those who get it don't get to keep it."

They aren't alone in feeling this way. Comments below the item's listing on the Wowhead database are equally scorching. "I love FOMO in their explicitly non-fomo game," wrote user TheWhiteRose.

"Just... Why?" added user Darrenic427. "They could very easily just patch out the camp buff duration and keep the visual effect, but Blizzard just doesn't like pretty fire I guess. Figures that they finally give us access to purple fire but then take it away after a month."

The battle between collectors and time-limited FOMO items is one that has been waged for about as long as these sorts of items have been a part of games. Though for the pouch, it's an especially weird case: an item that's cool to have but so temporary in nature that it makes it both important to completionists and strangely pointless to care about. Whether it makes a return in a later update for World of Warcraft: Forever and doesn't require out-of-game actions to obtain, and doesn't disappear, we'll have to wait and see.

WoW Forever itself is proving popular among players - me included. It's added a staggering amount of new quests and many new features to the original version of World of Warcraft, which, in turn, has injected the game with an impressive amount of new items to collect. Completionists will likely be glued to the game for a long time.

Official Dungeons & Dragons online toolset D&D Beyond was involved in a major cyber attack this week, but promises that user payment details were not impacted.

Replying to a Reddit thread reporting on the breach, D&D Beyond executive producer Brian Perry confirmed that the site was one of many hit by a widespread security incident earlier this week. However, because payments are handled via a separate provider, customer payment details were "not affected."

"Earlier this week, a third-party service provider experienced a security incident that affected a number of websites, including D&D Beyond," Perry writes. "We acted quickly to remove the service from our site, and our team has been reviewing the situation carefully since.

"Payments on D&D Beyond are handled through our secure payment provider and were not affected. If our review finds that any player needs to take action, we'll contact them directly.

"Thanks for being part of our community. We'll share an update if there's anything more you need to know."

According to the report by D&D Fantatic, which spotted the issue early, D&D Beyond was one of nearly 200 websites impacted by the malware attack - including sister site MTG Secret Lair, which just revealed a new Dune drop. This is because the attack "exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely, a third-party website testing tool." This has apparently been fixed, and the exploit has since been removed.

It's certainly a relief that D&D Beyond users don't need to worry about their bank details being skimmed, especially this month; the game just launched its latest and much-hyped book, D&D World of Warcraft (which I felt lived up to the promise, personally). Thankfully, anyone who invested in it via D&D Beyond doesn't need to panic - it looks like we can enjoy our adventures across Azeroth in peace.

#3839. Archetype go all in on the Mass Effect vibes with a FemJun reveal, but I'm just left hoping they'll call the alternative option MascJun to balance it out

I know it, you know it, hell, I'm sure developer Archetype Entertainment know it: Exodus is kind of just Mass Effect again. That's in part because the DNA of the game has been built by series vets like Drew Karpyshyn, Chad Robertson and James Ohlen. But it's also because, well, they're putting FemShep in the game. Yes, I'm being a tad facetious here, but when the latest trailer for your game is literally titled "Female Jun Reveal," well, comparisons will be made!

To top it all off, a blog post from the devs literally refers to the alternate gender for the protag as FemJun. They know what they're doing. In any case, first up, her voice actor! She's being played by Carina Conti, an up and comer last digitally heard in Mafia: The Old Country as Isabella Torrisi. Male Jun (who hasn't been given a nickname, which couldn't possibly serve to other female Jun (and MascJun is right there!)) has also had his voice actor confirmed as Stephen Oyoung, who you'll have heard as Mister Negative in Insomniac's Spider-Man games and Red Hood in Gotham Knights.

It's been previously confirmed that no matter which gender you pick for Jun, you'll be able to romance whoever you like, so, happy smoochin'! The story will stay the same too, as will dialogue options, though I'm imagine some pronoun switcheroos will take place somewhere along the line.

I'm mostly just left feeling that this doesn't really seem like it'll fix the game's boring hero problem. Edwin made note of Jun's quite lacklustre vibe earlier this year, aptly tearing down MascJun's Instagram visage, though this was prior to the face model and voice actor change the character has undergone. Personally, I'm not sure that'll be enough, and FemJun kind of matches that Instagram look; the perfect bun and bangs that pop out when she takes her helmet off is quite silly too. Ah well! A game isn't done until it's done (which, in theory, will be April 7th next year).

The saga of MindsEye has been somewhat concerning to watch from a distance. Originally pretty interesting, given it was headed up by former Rockstar North president Leslie Benzies, it instead became a poorly-received videogame (this is me being polite). One which would be a shame under any other circumstances, but has since spun out into a trainwreck saga involving multiple layoffs and, most notably, a lot of finger-pointing at alleged "saboteurs".

Many of its actual developers happen to disagree, a whopping 93 of them alleging "systemic mistreatment, mismanagement, and mishandling of the redundancy process" back in October of last year. The studio itself has continued to try and update it, including with a mission that is about those alleged saboteurs, which is a normal thing you do when you are trying to be taken seriously.

Anyway, the layoffs are continuing, and it looks like it's sink or swim for Build a Rocket Boy. Things have never gotten sinkier or swimmier than right now, however, as both a statement of affairs and a notice of administrator's proposal filed November 16 (and unlocked yesterday) have painted a picture, as spotted by RedbullCola on ResetEra.

Build a Rocket Boy has an unsecured creditor claim—that is to say, debt—of around £61 million: "Unsecured creditor claims are presently estimated at approximately £61.752 million, principally comprising amounts due to group undertakings, Diameter, NetEase and various trade creditors."

Unsurprisingly, Build a Rocket Boy is still hooked on the saboteurs thing: "The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary. The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties."

The plan? Sue the pants off everybody. "The Company had undertaken detailed investigations and had commenced litigation against several third parties, with the assistance of the Company's former legal advisers, Brandsmiths, in connection with matters described earlier in the Proposals. The Joint Administrators consider the litigation potentially to be the largest asset of the Administration."

It's that last bit: "Largest asset". When your largest asset is the hypothetical money that'll come from the pendulum of justice finally swinging your way, you're in deep trouble. And given how little concrete evidence has emerged so far of a wider conspiracy against a game we gave an honest shot and just found to be plain bad? I do not think this is going to work.

Publisher Aniplex and developer TYPE-MOON have released visual novel Witch on the Holy Night for iOS via App Store and Android via Google Play in Japan for 2,900 yen.

Witch on the Holy Night has previously been released for PlayStation 4, Switch, and PC via Steam. Shipments and digital sales have surpassed 500,000 units worldwide.

Here is an overview of the game, via Aniplex:

Experience a young adult tale, set in the vibrant and bustling 1980s, that follows an innocent young man and two young “witches.”

Two witches dwell within a mansion atop a hill.

It is the late 1980s, the twilight years of a vibrant and bustling era. A boy arrives in the city only to encounter two witches living in the present day.

The boy leads a normal life. One of the girls is proud and dignified. The other lives hidden away, as if in slumber.

Three stars in parallel orbit, fated never to meet. The story of how these three completely different characters come to live under one roof will soon be revealed…

First released in 2012 for PC, Witch on the Holy Night returns after 10 years, further refined with fully voiced characters and a full high-definition visual remaster.

#3836. UK Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch is more worried "about the amount of time" people will spend on GTA 6 than the game's violent content

"I remember in my childhood playing Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter. I didn't hit anybody after playing those games."

Leader of the UK Conservative Party (and former Mortal Kombat player) Kemi Badenoch is more worried about the amount of time people will spend playing GTA 6 rather than the game itself.

Every new Grand Theft Auto game invites some amount of controversy over its in-game violence or depictions of sex and drugs - from San Andreas' raunchy Hot Coffee mini-game to GTA 5's graphic torture scene. Ahead of GTA 6's release this week, the Tory leader downplayed those fears.

"I would be more worried about the amount of time people were spending on a game than the game specifically. I remember in my childhood playing Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter. I didn't hit anybody after playing those games," Badenoch said in a news conference shared by Sky News (good spot, IGN).

While Badenoch's stance might be surprising for the normally right-wing UK political party, she did still worry over children who might play GTA 6 for too long. There are probably far worse ways for kids to spend their time than engaging with a long-form story like GTA 6's, though, especially in an era with endless amounts of 10-second clips to mindlessly scroll past and declining funding into youth programs.

"I haven't played Grand Theft Auto, I know people are worried about the game content. At the same time, I'd be more worried about a kid who played it all day, who was in their bedroom all day, than one who spends half an hour on it and then went out and did something else. They are two different things," Badenoch added.

GTA 6's release is imminent and is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time. One analyst even suggested GTA 6 could make over $2bn in its opening weekend - that's handily more money than Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey made during its entire run in cinemas, for context.

If you'd like to reminisce a bit before the long-awaited game finally hits, you can check out our favourite Grand Theft Auto pieces Eurogamer's published over the years.

#3835. Mondrayn is a putrid, crunchy pixel art RPG about escaping from limbo where "dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering"

Everything's a bit grim these days, so let's just go all in on the misery shall we? Let's start with this line from the game's Steam page we'll be talking about today: "Mondrayn is a grim JRPG with survival elements where dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering." Crikey! You're telling me the sweet release of death won't be so saccharine after all? Sounds rough, so it's a good thing Mondrayn looks so darn compelling.

The world of Mondrayn is a dead one. You start out waking up in a city, it's in a gnarly state, of course, overrun by a disease of unknown origin. Horrible monsters are roaming about the place, cults are performing nasty rituals, and you've got no memories, so all you can do is try and make any friends you can, kill the undead and get out of, all places, limbo.

Mondrayn is an RPG in the sense that it utilises turn-based combat, "intertwined with shootouts." I'm not entirely sure how that manifests, you do seem to be able to do both regular attacks and special moves, the state of characters seems to have an impact, but truthfully I don't mind not understanding because what I'm here for are the utterly, delectably rancid vibes on display.

Every single pixel in this game looks like it was dipped in a vat of grime, puss, blood and vomit, and I revel in it! The enemy portraits are crunchy and violet, they look ripped straight out of some obscure art book for a Warhammer-esque tabletop game no one has ever heard of. It looks a bit fantasy, a bit steampunk, and incredibly, incredibly grimdark. It's the kind of world I'd rather instantly top myself than spend a second longer in, so, kudos to the fictional characters in it that have no choice in the matter for managing better than me. As it stands, Mondrayn has no release date, but you can wishlist it on Steam in the meantime.

Your choice to spare or kill Arnold in GTA 6 has consequences

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

In the mission 'Hey Arnold!' you face the story's first major moral dilemma: do you kill or spare Arnold in GTA 6? After Brian's shady business associate, Arnold, goes dark during GTA 6 Chapter 1, Jason, Brian, and Cal hunt him down to the radar station near the Aerostat. It turns out Arnold isn't very happy with Brian's drug-dealing tactics and, after some heated words, Arnold and his goons jump into a pickup truck and speed off.

But no one disrespects Brian like that, not on Jason's watch, and a high speed car chase immediately ensues. When the chase ends, you must choose whether to let Arnold live or execute him, with your choice impacting your GTA 6 criminal profile.

If you continue chasing Arnold to the Key Lento Marina, he abandons his vehicle and Brian tells Jason to "shut him up." Though, he doesn't specify how. He simply says: "Do whatever you have to do." You then need to chase after Arnold on foot (hopefully you've been working on your fitness) until you get close enough to tackle him or he reaches the end of the pier and has nowhere else to run. He then begins to beg Jason for his life.

To spare Arnold, hold down L2/LT to interact with him and press X/A to select the option to 'Spare' him. Instead of killing Arnold, Jason will threaten him and let him go. In return, you receive a contribution toward the Restrained criminal profile and Arnold scuttles off, with Brian none the wiser.

There are two ways you can kill Arnold in this GTA 6 mission. The first is to complete the car chase to the Marina and then follow Arnold on foot until he reaches the end of the pier or you're able tackle him to the ground. However, when he starts begging for his life, you can instead execute him with your weapon. If you do this, you receive a warning that "Indiscriminate violence will contribute toward a violent criminal profile."

If you'd rather not deal with Arnold's begging – or a pesky foot chase – you can kill Arnold by shooting at his vehicle and/or him during the car chase. Killing Arnold in this way is quicker, but contributes toward a Ruthless criminal profile.

Whichever choice you make, the following cutscene will be the same.

Now imagine how many of those bad boys you can shove into a data center.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

You may not be able to buy memory right now, but the good news for a hopeful future is there's potentially quicker and smaller RAM on the horizon. JEDEC, the council that sets industry standards for RAM, has published a preview of what DDR6 could look like, and it seems like it will be itty and bitty.

According to JEDEC, DDR6 will bring with it higher bandwidth, higher capacities, better reliability, more energy efficiency, and different form factors (via VideoCardz).

Starting with bandwidth, DDR6 RDIMMs will start at a speed of 12.8 GT/s and are set to move up to "14.4 GT/s and beyond." DDR5 maxes out at 9.2 GT/s, representing a sizable bump. It also expands the data bus from 64 to 96 DQ, which no doubt contributes to the bandwidth increase.

That is fast, though not two times faster like DDR5 versus DDR4. It is worth noting, however, that memory modules tend to get faster over their lifetime so we don't know where that might end up.

The module for DDR6 is now 74 mm, which is almost half of the 133 mm for DDR5. This is supposedly "intended to help accommodate higher system memory density", with DDR6 supporting up to 128 GB DRAM die density (double that of DDR5).

There are other gains to be had with DDR6 too. JEDEC says it targets an improved performance-per-watt over DDR5 "through a change to VSS-terminated IO and data-center-focused low power modes"

JEDEC says DDR6 can support a "breadth of form factors", including RDIMM, UDIMM, CAMM.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

Now for one thing you may not want to hear, but might have already suspected: JEDEC says DDR6 is 'built for the data center". It says its interface is "optimised for high-capacity modules with configurations oriented to general purpose compute as well as AI inferencing and agentic AI, which demand more capacity and performance close to the CPU."

Being built for data center usage does not mean consumers will be left out in the cold, of course, but it does further signal just how much memory is being designed for future AI usage. And the memory crisis seems set to last at least through 2027, even if Acer's CEO reckons it's impossible for it to last until 2030. It is all heavily reliant on how much memory supply can be ramped up and how much memory demand comes from the AI boom, which is certainly a hard-to-predict industry.

Continuing the trend of news you don't want to hear, we don't know when DDR6 is supposed to be available to the public. It seems like the release window is between 2028 and 2029, but we don't have any more information than that. And that's before musing on whether we non-AI data center owners will ever be able to afford the module. Hopefully, the memory crisis will cool off in a couple of years, and DDR6 will actually be affordable for PC gamers, though whether it will be relevant for PC gaming is a whole other thing. But, to steal a line from The Shawshank Redemption, "Hope is a dangerous thing".

#3831. The siren call of user-generated content has caught Dead by Daylight in its snare, as Behaviour Interactive outline a big revamp update slated for next year

Weather, new models, better maps, it'll have it all

The promise of user-generated content, this idea that you could host a platform that grows infinitely because the people that interact with it make things for it and you don't even have to pay anyone, is an alluring one. And its siren call has come for Dead by Daylight, as developer Behaviour Interactive have outlined the future of the game, which includes a way to make your own bits for the multiplayer horror game.

"What if you could create your own Dead by Daylight experiences?" explains a blog post recapping the plans for how the game is going to change. "As one of the most exciting updates coming in 2027, the Dead by Daylight Workshop will open the doors to user-created content in some incredible ways. From designing your own Maps and importing custom assets, to modifying game rules, objectives, and even creating entirely new modes, the possibilities are vast."

The post goes on to note that anything created in the workshop will "exist separately from all our classic modes, with dedicated creation tools and moderation provided to ensure experienced modders have everything they need to do their best work, and all submissions meet our official guidelines." I am always hesitant when it comes to UGC faff, because the ability to make your own custom Debbie Daylight maps might sound promising, but people do actually have to engage with them for the whole thing to work. It's just putting a hat on a hat!

Anyway, the workshop isn't the only thing Behaviour have in the works. For one, the game is getting a big visual overhaul. You can expect lighting improvements, more detailed assets and "tons of atmospheric touches," alongside revamps of particular maps like the Temple of Purgation and Backwater Swamp. Killers and survivors will be getting some TLC too by "improving character textures, proportions, hair, and animations to make them look and feel more lifelike. That includes updated character rigs, new motion capture, and new facial animation technology designed to better express a character’s fear, pain, and struggles over the course of a Trial."

Beyond all of that, a dynamic weather system is coming to the game, meaning you'll now have to deal with the likes of rain, thunderstorms, snow and heavy wind, all of which can impact matches. Onboarding for newer folks should be getting some improvements too, with the addition of a "more cinematic introduction, clearer explanations and tutorials of game mechanics, and a more gradual introduction," to the game. All of this will be coming in one big update sometime in 2027, so, keep your eyes peeled for whenever that drops.

#3830. Original GTA 6 leaker pleads guilty to hacking Rockstar Games, years after first revealing Lucia

The 21-year-old responsible for hacking Rockstar Games and leaking in-development GTA 6 footage in 2022 has pleaded guilty to a number of offenses.

The GTA 6 leaker was initially sentenced to an indefinite stay at a hospital due to his severe autism, but was more recently deemed fit for trial and moved to a regular prison earlier this January. On Monday, at the Woolwich Crown Court in South East London, he pleaded guilty to hacking Rockstar Games and a number of other companies, including Uber and EE/BT, in cyber attacks estimated to have caused £10m in damages.

At the time of his Rockstar hack - when he was between the ages of 16 and 17 - the leaker was already under police protection at a Travelodge hotel to keep him from rival hackers he had allegedly stolen Bitcoin from. Somewhat surprisingly, he then managed to hack the multi-billion dollar game maker with nothing but an Amazon Fire Stick, the hotel room's TV and a bluetooth-connected keyboard and mouse.

As the BBC reports, he also managed to break into the developer's Slack channels, before threatening to release the GTA 6 source code if Rockstar failed to contact him within the day. The leaker has yet to be sentenced.

Those 2022 leaks were quite substantial, too, revealing about an hour of unfinished gameplay and clueing the world in on Lucia's existence - the series' first female protagonist in years. Of course, those 2022 leaks shouldn't be confused with 2026's, which saw Cyberleek spill nuggets of nearly finished clips onto the internet, despite Rockstar's best efforts to keep GTA 6 a closely guarded secret.

"We recently suffered a network intrusion in which an unauthorised third-party illegally accessed and downloaded confidential information from our systems, including early development footage for the next Grand Theft Auto," Rockstar said at the time, before it had officially unveiled GTA 6. "At this time we do not anticipate any disruption to our live game services, nor any long-term effect on the development of our ongoing projects. We are extremely disappointed to have any details of our next game shared with you all in this way."

Four years later, GTA 6 is finally around the corner - you're probably already aware considering the marketing frenzy Rockstar's been drumming up.

#3828. Slow down a bit and help a cow find a friend in the lush-looking, hand-drawn, milk deliver-em-up Milki Delivery, which is out now

I don't want to write about video games any more, I want to deliver milk in the countryside and hang out with a cow and quirky people! Sorry, what, there's a game all about that called Milki Delivery that came out today? Alright, I'll write about video games again, especially when they look as charming as this one does.

The stakes at play in Milki Delivery are very low (as are the steaks, no butchery to be found here, only one very sweet looking cow I couldn't possibly slaughter). You play as Neha, and she's made a promise to her pet cow, the titular Milki, that you'll find her a friend (I think this is a world where there aren't any cows left; yikes!). To do that, all you have to do is deliver her milk! Accept because this is an adventure game, you'll have to help out a few folks along the way.

It's a game very much about the journey, as when riding about this lush and bright countryside, you might find a group of cats that just need a little taste of that sweet creamy juice you've got. Or maybe you have some rope that a farmer needs to wrassle up some sheep. Sometimes you'll have to get a bit more involved with the various people you meet, but predominantly, you'll be delivering milk to folks who need it.

Getting around the place is quite simple too, you plot out your path ahead of time and let the game take you as it's all mouse driven. A relaxed experience to be sure, but the game's art is just so delightful to look at, I'm quite enticed by the idea of just slowing down and enjoying some pretty pictures and making friends along the way. You can make different kinds of milk, too, just be feeding Milki different ingredients. Not how that works in real life, but now I kind of wish it was.

In any case, Milki Delivery is out now, and you can pick it up on Steam.

#3827. Star Wars: Galactic Racer is getting much-requested split-screen multiplayer and new mode in 2027

The surprisingly awesome arcade podracing game Star Wars: Galactic Racer is getting split-screen multiplayer next year after loud fan requests, developer Fuse Games has announced.

Split-screen racing comes as part of an entirely new mode called Free Play that'll also allow players to mix and match vehicles, characters, tracks and planets in a galaxy far, far away. So, maybe don't expect to bring friends into the game's vast, pre-existing suite of modes just yet.

"We heard you," the studio wrote on social media. "Local split-screen multiplayer racing is coming in early 2027. A dedicated team at Fuse Games has been working hard to bring a brand new mode, Free Play, to Star Wars: Galactic Racer. This new mode will allow you to choose your vehicle, character, planet, and race track to race alone or with up to 3 other players in local split-screen action."

We’ve heard you! Local split-screen multiplayer racing is coming in early 2027. A dedicated team at @Fuse_Games has been working hard to bring a brand new mode, Free Play, to STAR WARS: Galactic Racer™. This new mode will allow you to choose your vehicle, character, planet, and race track to race alone or with up to 3 other players in local split-screen action.

Galactic Racer already has a pretty good selection of online multiplayer modes, like the 12-player speeder races and 8-player podracing tours, but there's currently no way to play with your mates in the same room.

Chris Donlan loved the thrilling racing game for mixing the best bits of Star Wars and Burnout - Fuse Games does have plenty of old Criterion DNA, mind you. "It's new games, with Roguelite choices and endless unlockables, and it's also old games, with cruel and ingenious courses where everything can be lost in an instant. It's a Galaxy Far, Far Away, and it's also Paradise City," he wrote in Eurogamer's five-star review.

With Galactic Racer and Zero Company under its belt, Lucasfilm Games said it's now "more flexible" about which developers it accepts pitches from. Hopefully, that'll lead to even more interesting games set in Star Wars' ultra flexible world.

One of the first things GTA 6 players searched for was strip club locations—genuinely, data doesn't lie. So, as a responsible guide writer, I loaded up the game and proceeded to spend my initial hours beelining around Leonida's hotspots. There are a few different strip clubs in Leonida, each with their own price range and different activities to try (that sounds sordid, but I'm also talking about, like, pool tables).

There are three strip clubs in the game I've found, plus a load of other night spots, like the Rusty Anchor close to where Jason starts, that have drinking and other activities, too.

This fancy strip club in downtown Vice City is the classiest option you have available, but also the priciest. It's quite easy to get here, even from Leonida Keys where Jason starts—just drive along route 1 towards Hamlet, merge onto route 97, and head north into Downtown. The clubs are just to the right of the giant crossroads route interchange in west Vice City. NINE1NINE itself is next door to The Vault club. This is the best option if you have a lot of money to burn, but also it feels a bit too fancy.

If you want a private dance, same as with previous GTA games, you just need to greet the dancer in question and then use the interaction icon to pay for it. Since this club is fancier, you can also get a private dance by interacting with the person by the entrance to the private rooms.

I appreciated NINE1NINE's lively club atmosphere, but I also ran out of cash very fast. Maybe one to try later in the game when you're a lot richer.

This strip club in Vice City's Crosstown is directly north from NINE1NINE, but there's a catch: this place only unlocks via the main story. I assume it's Chapter 3, considering that's when you meet its owner, but either way, it'll be a while before you can visit this establishment.

I assume in terms of price range, it's fancier than Delights (the cheapest option), but less fancy than NINE1NINE. This club gets one star because it wouldn't let me in, though maybe I'll change this review once I actually get inside.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Delights in Port Gellhorn is your cheapest option and it's a bit more rough and ready relative to NINE1NINE. It's also a long drive if you're just starting the game and want to visit the club in the northwest of the map. You'll want to drive to Hamlet via route 1 from the Keys, as with NINE1NINE, but then head northwest on route 82 towards Capri, then 103 merging onto the 404, past the airport towards Port Gellhorn. Bank a right when you reach the town, and the big Delights billboard to find it a little way further, on your left.

This club has stage dancing, unlike NINE1NINE, pool tables, but also cheaper private dances, tips, and drinks. Hilariously, some of the dancers also already know Jason and will actually make comments about him. I went here early in the game and one of the dancers mentioned Jason and Lucia, so I guess he must be a regular. In general, this club has a lot more character than the others, it's reasonably priced, also you can play pool—four stars. I also witnessed an old woman on a mobility scooter mugging someone outside, which gave added entertainment value.

#3825. Ex-Nvidia boss Jensen Huang offers to return if that's best for the company and America, Nvidia board essentially say 'nah, we're all good'

New rulers impervious to highly persuasive message of 'come on, please give me my job back, go USA'

Nvidia's board have indicated that they aren't about to do a big u-turn and reappoint recently resigned CEO Jensen Huang, following his departure after multiple alleged instances of extramarital cavorting were reported by the press. Since his exit last week, Huang has indicated he'd be open to making such a return, were it deemed best for both the company and AMERICA.

"On November 12th, our board of directors announced that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member," Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said during an investors call on November 17th (thanks, Percieving Calls Gamer). "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO."

That last bit seems likely to have been said with the intention of quieting down some of the speculation around a Huang return that's been bubbling away since he removed his bum from the black and green throne and that the exec embraced in a statement put out yesterday. "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life," he wrote. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the board’s independent investigation.

"Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. Nvidia is a once-in-a-generation company. If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO."

For now at least, it seems leather jacketed GPUperman will not be triumphantly flying back into his former post amid a wave of corporate and patriotic fervour. Likely as part of continued efforts to reassure moneyfolk that they won't be making negative headlines again soon following Huang's departure, Nvidia's board announced yesterday that they're establishing a "new standing committee responsible for board-level oversight of the company’s national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management". One of Huang's alleged affairs was with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The Chinese government have denied the accusations of espionage.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress is currently serving as Nvidia's interim CEO while the company's board searches for a permanent sexy leather jacket man replacement.

#3824. EA really doesn't want you to delete Madden NFL 27 to make room for GTA 6

"Don't let 210GB get between you and your league."

Assuming you didn't just buy a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X/S to play Grand Theft Auto 6, your console's limited storage space is likely already strained, meaning tough choices may have to be made to make room for Rockstar's chonky 212GB crime game.

In a move I don't remember seeing before, EA is asking players to spare Madden NFL 27 from the purge to free up console storage space. As spotted by Push Square, a desperate in-game message pops up when you launch the American Football game, pleading with you not to delete it.

The message highlights 17th November as the date of a Madden NFL 27 update, though its styling, wording and choice of background seem to hint at GTA 6.

"Don't delete!" it reads, as shared by Zirksee on X. "[Encrypted Signal] The target is locked. The crew is assembling for a high-stakes run. Await the signal from our insider on 11/17… do not leak this transmission."

EA's language and intention, however, are much clearer in this post on X, which specifically references GTA 6's large file size in a cheeky way, seemingly promoting the same update.

"Don't let 210GB get between you and your league," the post reads, clearly quoting GTA 6's file size.

The update in question is fairly notable, adding a Madden 97 throwback with era-appropriate players, playbooks and what looks to be 16-bit visuals. Though it's obviously not related to GTA 6 in any way, it's easy to see why EA would fear a significant drop in players once Rockstar's game arrives, something other publishers are undoubtedly worried about.

As part of a recent restructuring, EA laid off 400 employees, closed down BioWare, cancelled unannounced projects and revealed a refocusing on its core franchises and biggest monkey-makers. That includes EA Sports, of course, where a team is currently developing a game codenamed Project Gridiron, described as "a social-first open-world experience for our American Football team".
